[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Introduction to MongoDB Replication"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Replication in MongoDB provides high availability and data redundancy. It involves creating multiple copies of your data across different servers. If one server fails, another server can take over, ensuring continuous operation and preventing data loss."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Key Concepts"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Replica Set: A group of MongoDB server instances that maintain the same data set. It includes one primary node and multiple secondary nodes."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Primary Node: The main server in a replica set that receives all write operations. It then replicates these operations to the secondary nodes."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Secondary Nodes: Servers in a replica set that replicate data from the primary node. They can handle read operations and become the primary if the current primary fails."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Automatic Failover: If the primary node becomes unavailable, the replica set automatically elects a new primary from the secondary nodes."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Data Redundancy: Replication ensures that your data is stored on multiple servers, protecting against data loss due to hardware failures or other issues."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Benefits of Replication"},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"High Availability: Ensures that your application remains available even if one or more servers fail."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Data Redundancy: Protects against data loss by storing multiple copies of your data."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Read Scalability: Secondary nodes can handle read operations, distributing the load and improving performance."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Disaster Recovery: Provides a mechanism for recovering data in the event of a disaster."},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Setting up a Replica Set"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"To set up a replica set, you need to configure each MongoDB instance to be part of the set. This involves specifying the replica set name and the other members of the set."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"# Start MongoDB instances with the --replSet option
mongod --replSet "myReplicaSet" --port 27017 --dbpath /data/db/rs1
mongod --replSet "myReplicaSet" --port 27018 --dbpath /data/db/rs2
mongod --replSet "myReplicaSet" --port 27019 --dbpath /data/db/rs3"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"After starting the instances, connect to one of them using the MongoDB shell and initiate the replica set."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"# Connect to one of the instances
mongo --port 27017

# Initiate the replica set
rs.initiate( {
   _id : "myReplicaSet",
   members: [
      { _id : 0, host : "localhost:27017" },
      { _id : 1, host : "localhost:27018" },
      { _id : 2, host : "localhost:27019" }
   ]
})"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can check the status of the replica set using the 'rs.status()' command."},{"order":20,"type":"code","text":"# Check the replica set status
rs.status()"},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Replication is a crucial feature in MongoDB for ensuring high availability, data redundancy, and read scalability. By setting up a replica set, you can protect your data and ensure continuous operation of your application."}]
